<div class="sheet">
  <div class="ws-head">
    <div>
      <h1>Transition Risk Register — Six Predictable Failure Modes</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">A pre-mortem risk register completed before work starts, with an owner and a named early-warning signal per risk.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-08-pitfall-risk-register</b><br>
      Pack G - The plan we leave with<br>
      fill order <b>8</b> &middot; type <b>diagnostic</b><br>
      audience <b>mixed</b>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>Planning the Transition</b>, <i>Common Transition Pitfalls</i> &middot;
    <code>handbook\ch08-planning-the-transition.qmd</code> L240-252 &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch08-planning-the-transition.html#sec-transition-pitfalls">#sec-transition-pitfalls</a>
  </div>
  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Work through each risk. Score likelihood silently and individually first; record the signal you would actually see, where it appears, and one named watcher. Point to the mitigation already funded in the roadmap. High likelihood: already seen here or a named precondition exists today. Medium: no precedent here, but no current practice would prevent it. Low: a named existing control would catch it before harm; name that control or the rating is not Low. Impact: Critical means codebase corruption or a trust-boundary crossing, discovered late or not at all; High means a wave or sprint of rework, or loss of the room's confidence in the program; Medium means hours of cost, visible at the next checkpoint; Low means an irritation absorbed in the normal loop. Band 1 = High likelihood with Critical or High impact; Band 2 = any other pairing containing Critical or High impact; Band 3 = everything else.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-head"><div><h1>Transition Risk Register — Six Predictable Failure Modes</h1><p class="ws-sub">Organization-specific risks, rows 7–8. Name each risk in your own words and diagnose it against the roadmap.</p></div><div class="ws-meta"><b>WS-08-pitfall-risk-register</b><br>Pack G - The plan we leave with<br>fill order <b>8</b> &middot; type <b>diagnostic</b><br>audience <b>mixed</b></div></div>
  <div class="ws-source">Source: <b>Planning the Transition</b>, <i>Common Transition Pitfalls</i> &middot; <code>handbook\ch08-planning-the-transition.qmd</code> L240-252 &middot; <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch08-planning-the-transition.html#sec-transition-pitfalls">#sec-transition-pitfalls</a></div>
  <div class="ws-instruction">Score likelihood silently and individually first; record the signal you would actually see, where it appears, and one named watcher. Point to the mitigation already funded in the roadmap. High likelihood: already seen here or a named precondition exists today. Medium: no precedent here, but no current practice would prevent it. Low: a named existing control would catch it before harm; name that control or the rating is not Low. Impact: Critical means codebase corruption or a trust-boundary crossing, discovered late or not at all; High means a wave or sprint of rework, or loss of the room's confidence in the program; Medium means hours of cost, visible at the next checkpoint; Low means an irritation absorbed in the normal loop. Band 1 = High likelihood with Critical or High impact; Band 2 = any other pairing containing Critical or High impact; Band 3 = everything else.</div>
